question.text: Water in a river of width 30 m flows downstream at a constant speed of 2 m/s. A boatman steers his boat at 5 m/s relative to the water, maintaining an angle of 37° with the direction of the river flow. Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The time taken by the boatman to cross over to the opposite bank.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: The total downstream drift of the boatman upon reaching the opposite bank.

conditions: rowing velocity relative to water = 5 m/s
rowing direction = 37° to the river flow

figure.description: A river of width 30 m flows horizontally to the right with speed 2 m/s. A boat's velocity vector of magnitude 5 m/s is oriented at an angle of 37° above the horizontal downstream direction. Its components are 4 m/s along the stream (plus the 2 m/s river speed, making 6 m/s horizontally) and 3 m/s perpendicular across the stream.

solution.approach: Split the rowing velocity into a part across the river and a part along it, then add the river current to the along part.

steps.text: Resolve the rowing velocity of 5 m/s at 37° into a part across the river and a part along the river.
steps.equation: v_across = 5 sin 37° = 3 m/s, v_along = 5 cos 37° = 4 m/s

steps.text: Only the across part carries the boat over the width of 30 m, so use it to find the crossing time.
Add the river current to the along part to get the total speed along the bank, then multiply by the time to get the drift.

common_mistakes.text: Using the full 5 m/s instead of only the across component 3 m/s gives a crossing time of 6 s.
Forgetting to add the river current to the along component gives a drift of 40 m instead of 60 m.
